# Story 11.3: E2E test for cookie + localStorage persistence across an app relaunch

Status: ready-for-dev

## Story

As a user (Dave),
I want end-to-end proof that my saved state survives quitting and reopening the desktop app,
so that I can trust login and preferences persist in real use, not just in unit tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An e2e spec launches the Electron app via Playwright's `_electron` harness (the pattern already used by `apps/electron/src/electron-package-launch.smoke.spec.ts`) with no `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` set, writes a known value to `localStorage` in the first window, then quits and relaunches the app. On relaunch it asserts the same origin is loaded and the previously-written `localStorage` value is still present — proving the origin (and therefore the storage partition) is stable across launches.
2. An e2e spec sets an auth/session cookie for the app origin in the first launch, quits and relaunches the app, then asserts the cookie is still present on the same origin after relaunch — so a logged-in session persists rather than being wiped by a new random port.
3. The existing Electron smoke spec (`apps/electron/src/electron-package-launch.smoke.spec.ts`) runs alongside the new persistence spec and all pass unchanged — no pre-existing test regresses, and the `DMS_SMOKE_PORT`-driven smoke path is unaffected by the fixed default introduced in Story 11.2.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [ ] Task 1: Add a relaunch-persistence e2e spec (AC: #1)
  - [ ] 1.1 Create `apps/electron/src/session-persistence.spec.ts` using Playwright's `_electron.launch(...)` harness, mirroring the launch/teardown pattern in `electron-package-launch.smoke.spec.ts`. Ensure no `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` is set for this spec so it exercises the fixed default origin.
  - [ ] 1.2 In the first window, write a known sentinel value to `localStorage` (e.g. via `page.evaluate(() => localStorage.setItem('dms_persist_probe', '...'))`).
  - [ ] 1.3 Quit the app (`electronApp.close()`), relaunch it, and assert the loaded URL origin is identical to the first launch's origin AND that `localStorage.getItem('dms_persist_probe')` returns the sentinel value.
- [ ] Task 2: Add a cookie-persistence assertion (AC: #2)
  - [ ] 2.1 In the same spec, set an auth/session cookie for the app origin in the first launch (e.g. via `context.addCookies(...)` or by exercising the login flow that sets the AD-5 secure cookie).
  - [ ] 2.2 After quit + relaunch, assert the cookie is still present on the same origin (read back via `context.cookies()`), proving the session persists across launches.
- [ ] Task 3: Verify no regression to the smoke spec (AC: #3)
  - [ ] 3.1 Run the new persistence spec and `electron-package-launch.smoke.spec.ts` together; confirm both pass and the smoke path (which sets `DMS_SMOKE_PORT`) is unaffected by the fixed default.

## Dev Notes

- **Why this e2e exists:** Story 11.1/11.2 prove at unit level that the resolved port is a stable constant. This spec proves the *user-visible* outcome — that cookies and localStorage actually survive a real quit + relaunch of the packaged/dev Electron app, which is what the Epic prose asks for ("ensure cookies are properly saved and retrieved within the electron environment").
- **Governing ADs:** AD-5 (Auth: Cognito JWT + CSRF, secure cookie) — the auth cookie must persist; AD-10 (Electron thin wrapper). FR-19 (Auth/session → `routes/auth/` + `plugins/`, client `auth/`).
- **Harness reference:** reuse the `_electron.launch(...)` invocation, app-path resolution, and teardown from `apps/electron/src/electron-package-launch.smoke.spec.ts`. Do not set `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` in this spec — it must exercise the fixed default origin that Story 11.2 introduces.
- **Cookie note:** the AD-5 auth cookie is set with `secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` (`apps/server/src/app/routes/auth/set-secure-cookie.function.ts`). Over a plain `http://localhost:<port>` origin in dev, `secure` cookies are not stored — so for AC #2 prefer setting a non-secure session cookie directly via the Playwright context (or run against the production-equivalent config) to avoid a false negative. The point of the test is *origin stability across relaunch*, not the secure flag.
- **Testing standard:** Electron e2e runs under the project's existing Playwright/electron runner. Keep the spec self-contained and deterministic; clean up any probe keys it writes.
